messages:
Samir: noticing a sustained throughput drop (~35%) on pool-gpu-ff2 since 02:10 UTC, lots of worker restarts and a spike in GPU OOMs. rolling alert: @oncall please triage
Maria: saw the same, p95 latency jumped from 220ms -> 740ms. charts show request rate roughly steady but tokens/sec down.
Tess: I pulled logs from the autoscaler; it didn't scale up. a bunch of workers restarted with OOMs, then some kernel fallback messages.
Dan: paste of recent runtime log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T02:11:03Z] worker-47 ERROR: cuda runtime call failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T02:11:03Z] kernel-selector INFO: selected kernel=fast_attention_v3 for model=llama-30b seq=2048
[2026-03-15T02:11:03Z] kvcache-manager WARN: eviction pressure high, evicted 412 entries
[2026-03-15T02:11:04Z] kernel-selector INFO: fallback kernel=generic_attention_seq for model=llama-30b seq=2048 due to alloc failure
[2026-03-15T02:11:04Z] worker-47 INFO: restarting after OOM
```
Samir: interesting that selector chose fast_attention_v3—should be memory-hungry at seq=2048. Was there a recent rule change?
Maria: there was a perf rollout yesterday that updated kernel heuristics to favor v3 for throughput at medium seq lengths (PR 0x3f2b). Could be the regression.
Tess: I ran a quick profiler on a repro job (seq=2048, batch=4). Before PR: 4.6 tokens/ms, after PR: 5.2 tokens/ms but memory high and intermittent failures. Kernel v3 alloc map: peak GPU mem 28.1GB (device has 32GB). With KV caching under multi-tenant load it hits fragmentation.
Dan: profiler snippet (aggregate):
```
kernel fast_attention_v3: avg_time=9.2ms, mem=7.3GB
kernel generic_attention_seq: avg_time=12.1ms, mem=4.1GB
KVCache usage: base=6.8GB, delta=+3.5GB per request pattern
Evictions: spikes at 02:10:40 -> 02:11:10 correlated with tenant B burst
```
Samir: tenant B is noisy-tenant-17; they had a spike of many long seq chats. This pushed slab allocator into fragmentation -> OOM on fast kernels.
Maria: are there existing mitigations? auto-fallback exists but fallback increases latency sharply and causes restarts under backpressure.
Tess: short-term: pin the kernel heuristic to prefer generic_attention_seq for seq>=1024 on the affected pool. That should reduce memory per-request.
Dan: config patch I propose:
```yaml
name: kernel-heuristic-emergency
match: pool=gpu-ff2 and seq>=1024
action: prefer kernels [generic_attention_seq, aten_mha_v2]
priority: emergency
```
Samir: +1, roll to a single canary node first (node-ff2-canary1). monitor p95 and OOM count. Also add KVCache eviction threshold increase to avoid aggressive evictions that cause fragmentation.
Maria: opened alert dashboards and a short-lived evict-threshold override as discussed. I've also pinned noisy-tenant-17 to a lower priority queue (soft-rate-limit) to give breathing room.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: kernel-heuristic-emergency -> canary node-ff2-canary1. CI checks passed.
Tess: after applying on canary: p95 dropped from 740ms -> 320ms, tokens/sec recovered ~+28%, no new OOMs for 8 minutes. Good sign.
Dan: logs from canary after rollout:
```
[2026-03-15T02:18:05Z] kernel-selector INFO: forced preference generic_attention_seq for seq=2048
[2026-03-15T02:18:06Z] kvcache-manager INFO: eviction-threshold-overridden -> 0.85
[2026-03-15T02:18:07Z] worker-47 INFO: health ok
```
Samir: plan: roll to remaining pool within 20m if stable, open a follow-up issue to revisit kernel scoring to account for fragmentation/tenant burst profiles. Also schedule a deeper profiler run to model allocator behavior and slab churn.
Maria: filing follow-up: ISSUE-RED-314: kernel-selection should consider fragmentation score + tenant burstiness. Assigned to Tess + Dan.
Tess: note for postmortem: causal chain is noisy tenant burst -> KVCache growth + slab fragmentation -> kernel heuristic picks memory-optimized-for-speed kernel (v3) -> allocation failures -> fallback/restarts -> throughput drop.
Samir: good. adding a temporary runbook note and tagging ops handbook. Will monitor for 1h and then close incident if green. :thumbsup:
